evidence.requirements: Every functional requirement is met. The start page shows title, date/time, "EUR n per guest" and "<n> seats left" (Tastings.jsx:24-30, start.jpg). Each tasting has a "Book <title>" link (Tastings.jsx:30). The form has fields labelled Name/Email/Guests and a "Book" button (Book.jsx:100-136). Errors appear next to their field (form.jpg). The confirmation has the heading "Booking confirmed" plus tasting, guests, total and reference (Book.jsx:65-76, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.jsx:81-91, index.js:4). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, and a Cancel button frees the seats (app.js:82-96, staff.jpg). Fully booked tastings show "Fully booked" (Tastings.jsx:33). The app uses React with Express, react-router, react-hook-form and zod, and serves on PORT with default 3000. Partly met: (1) the success state is not visually distinct. The confirmation is a plain neutral panel with no success styling (confirmation.jpg), even though the brief asks for clear success states. (2) The process requirement (specify/plan/specs) has no artifacts in the repo, because .superpowers/sdd/.gitignore ignores everything.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and insert run synchronously with no await between them, so concurrent requests cannot overbook (bookings.js:27-35, tested in guest-api.test.js:82-88). Guests are validated as integers from 1 to 8; strings are converted but booleans and arrays are rejected (schemas.js:9-12). Name and email are trimmed with length limits. Unknown tastings return 404. Cancelling removes the booking, so seats are freed (bookings.js:37-42). Gaps: (1) after a 409, the "seats left" line on the form stays stale (Book.jsx:96), although the field error does show the current count. (2) Cancel has no confirmation step, so one mis-tap permanently deletes a guest's booking (Staff.jsx:129-136). (3) An expired session is only deleted when it is next checked, so the session Map grows over time (staff-auth.js:16-22). (4) In Staff.jsx:38, any failure during the initial load, such as a network error, silently shows the sign-in form.
evidence.security: React escapes all output and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Passwords are compared with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests (staff-auth.js:32-35). Session tokens are 32 random bytes stored server-side with an 8-hour TTL. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and Secure is set behind a trusted proxy (app.js:65-71). Sign-out revokes the session. Login is rate-limited (app.js:18-25). The JSON body is capped at 10kb, malformed JSON is handled without logging the body (app.js:100-104), and no secrets are in the code. Weaknesses: (1) the booking endpoint has no rate limit, so a script can book out every tasting. (2) No security headers are set (no helmet or CSP). (3) The IP-based login limiter can lock out all staff behind a proxy when TRUST_PROXY is not set. (4) Client URLs are not encoded with encodeURIComponent (api.js:23,27); this is harmless today because ids and references are fixed patterns.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: server/app.js for routes, bookings.js for the store, staff-auth.js for sessions, and one zod schema in shared/schemas.js used by both client and server. Pages are split into Tastings, Book and Staff, with a thin api.js. Names are clear and the comments explain why, not what (bookings.js:27, app.js:100, format.js:1). createApp takes injected options, which makes it testable. Minor issues: inline style objects (Book.jsx:98, Staff.jsx:79), and Staff.jsx manages view, notice and password with ad-hoc useState even though react-hook-form is used everywhere else.
evidence.tests: There are four node:test files with good server-side coverage: seat arithmetic, overbooking (409), concurrent last-seat booking, validation for each field including boundaries (0, 9, 2.5, "abc", boolean, array), unknown tasting, wrong and correct password, cookie flags, rate limit, session expiry, sign-out revocation, grouping, cancel freeing seats, SPA fallback, and logging of malformed JSON. There are no React or UI tests and no end-to-end tests. Nothing checks the labels, the "Book <title>" text, error placement next to the field, the confirmation content, or the fully booked rendering, even though the brief states these explicitly.
evidence.ux_design: The design is coherent and winery-appropriate: wine-red header with a gold rule, serif headings, cream background, card grid (start.jpg). The form is clean, with an inline red error under the email field and a visible gold focus ring (form.jpg). The staff table is readable, with an empty "No bookings yet" state (staff.jpg). The CSS is responsive with a 640px breakpoint and a scrolling table wrapper. Weak points: the confirmation looks plain, with no success colour or icon, and the dl is oddly indented (confirmation.jpg). There is no imagery or venue information, so the page looks generic. The staff view shows no seat totals per tasting, and cancelling needs no confirmation.
evidence.accessibility: Every input has a label. Errors use aria-invalid, aria-describedby and role=alert (Book.jsx:104-108). react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field (form.jpg). focus-visible outlines are set (styles.css:128). The page has lang=en, semantic main/nav/header/footer, th scope=col, sr-only text for the Actions column header, and descriptive aria-labels on the Cancel buttons. Muted text (#6e625d on cream) is roughly 5:1, which passes. Gaps: when the view switches to the confirmation, focus does not move and nothing is announced. The "Fully booked" notice in Book.jsx:87 has no role. Firing role=alert on several fields at once can be noisy for screen readers.
evidence.simplicity: There are 8 runtime dependencies, each with a clear purpose (express, rate-limit, react, react-dom, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, resolvers), plus vite. The whole app is about 600 lines with no needless abstraction. Bookings are kept in memory, as the brief allows.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, so no run, setup or environment instructions; STAFF_PASSWORD and TRUST_PROXY are documented only in a comment in server/index.js:5. There is no CI pipeline, no docs, ADRs or specs (spec folder gitignored), no staff manual and no changelog, and the version stays at 0.1.0. On the plus side, package-lock.json pins dependency versions and engines requires node >=22, though there is no .nvmrc and the range is open-ended. npm test, build and start work as scripts. The server tests give a regression net for the API. A built dist/ folder is included even though .gitignore lists it.

unmet_requirements: The look and feel only partly delivers a clear success state: the confirmation page is a plain neutral panel (confirmation.jpg)
The process requirement (specify, plan, spec tool) has no artifacts in the repository; the .superpowers/sdd folder is fully gitignored
strengths: Solid server logic: the synchronous seat check prevents overbooking (tested with concurrent requests), and one zod schema validates on both client and server with field-level errors
Careful staff security: a timing-safe password comparison, server-side random session tokens with TTL and revocation, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookies, a login rate limit, and no body logging
A lean, idiomatic stack (Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod) with a coherent winery-styled, responsive UI and good form accessibility
issues: No README, CI, docs or staff manual: run and setup steps and the STAFF_PASSWORD/TRUST_PROXY variables are only discoverable by reading the code
No UI or end-to-end tests: the exact labels, button texts, error placement, confirmation content and fully booked rendering the brief requires are untested

UX and robustness gaps: the confirmation has no success styling and gets no focus or announcement, staff Cancel needs no confirmation, and the booking endpoint has no rate limit, so a script could book out every tasting
review.verdict: The app meets the brief's functional requirements, with correct seat handling, careful staff authentication and a tidy winery look, and it is backed by thorough API tests. It is held back by having no README, CI or docs, no front-end tests, and a few UX gaps (plain confirmation, Cancel without confirmation), so it needs a short hardening pass before going to the winery.
